data.text: can you make research for how to manage the same features on other coding agents, not only claude
OPERATOR 2026-10-23 TE-Q1/Q3: "Yes to 1-hour TTL and the 240 s wait cap always"

OPERATOR 2026-10-23 TE-Q2/Q6/Q7: "Your defaults, but the user should also be able to select AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW option for claude (research for the same features for your questions for all the other coding agents) and if you detect that an agent cannot complete a task before compaction, you could extend the context window (while just informing the user with warning about it) until the coding or research task is completed, so the compaction will not degrade the performance."
OPERATOR 2026-10-23 TE-Q4/Q5/Q8: "Route to cheaper models or models we still have spending limit, check automatically if the limit is reset, and resume automatically if it is"

data.alternatives: Keep 5 minutes plus poll cadence only: rejected, leaves rewrites after any longer gap.
data.consequences: 1-hour writes cost 2x instead of 1.25x; needs Claude Code 2.1.242+ (older: UNAVAILABLE, not pass); plan-limit weighting checked by TE-verify.
data.context: Research: 52% of subagent spend is whole-context cache rewrites after waits over the 5-minute TTL.
data.decision: Yes (operator 2026-10-23: 'Yes to 1-hour TTL and the 240 s wait cap always'). Launcher env block and project settings set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h (or subagentPromptCacheTtl); doctor warns when unset.
data.title: Subagent prompt-cache TTL is one hour for every Claude Code agent ddflow launches

data.alternatives: Only when the 1h TTL is declined: rejected by the operator.
data.consequences: More short calls; no 570 s sleep loops in drivers; also protects hosts billing usage credits, which drop to 5 min TTL.
data.context: 583 rewrite events followed sleep loops averaging 11.7 min.
data.decision: Always, not only as fallback (operator 2026-10-23: 'Yes to 1-hour TTL and the 240 s wait cap always'). ddflow wait and driver poll recipes return still-waiting within [wait].max_call_seconds (default 240); the agent re-calls; heartbeat rides on it.
data.title: A single wait call never outlives 240 s, always

data.alternatives: Auto-compact only (window 300000): kept as the user-selectable option, loses ordering detail. Rotation only: rejected as sole mechanism by the operator.
data.consequences: Honest limit: a running client session usually cannot change its window mid-run (env/setting read at launch; Claude Code /autocompact is a user command), so extension is decided at launch or lane rotation from the task estimate; for the lead it is a recommendation. Larger windows cost more per call and per cache rewrite. Ceiling knob; company floors tighten-only.
data.context: Lead median context 402K; 39 agents grew past 200K; 12 agents with 300+ calls are 67% of subagent spend.
data.decision: Defaults accepted (operator 2026-10-23: 'Your defaults, but the user should also be able to select AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW option for claude ... and if you detect that an agent cannot complete a task before compaction, you could extend the context window (while just informing the user with warning about it) until the coding or research task is completed'). (1) Lanes rotate at 250K with a brief hand-off; lead compacts at a task boundary below 350K with a hand-off note. (2) The user may instead select an auto-compact window: Claude Code CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW (100K-1M tokens), setting autoCompactWindow, flag --autocompact, command /autocompact (verified in code.claude.com settings-reference and env-vars docs 2026-10-23; precedence env > flag > setting); CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE only lowers. Equivalent knobs for other agents: task TE-compact-window-per-agent. (3) Window extension: task CC-window-extend; separate operator-requested behaviour, not automatic rotation.
data.title: Context caps: lanes rotate at 250K, lead compacts at a task boundary below 350K; plus user-selectable auto-compact window and context-window extension

data.alternatives: Do not change models until an A/B finishes (the proposal default): rejected, limit stops cost more than the risk.
data.consequences: Needs a layered price/limit table in config; quality risk watched by the A/B; links P-operator-digest, P-batch-gates, P-context-compaction.
data.context: Fix lanes are 56% of subagent spend; all transcripts are one model so nothing was measured. The operator delegated this money decision.
data.decision: Route work to cheaper models or to models/subscriptions that still have spending headroom (operator 2026-10-23: 'Route to cheaper models or models we still have spending limit, check automatically if the limit is reset, and resume automatically if it is'). Mechanical items route by headroom immediately; a measured A/B stays as the quality check. Reviewers and design stay on the strongest available model that satisfies the cross-family rule. Tasks: TE-limit-aware-routing, amended TE-model-routing.
data.title: Model routing now: route by price and spending headroom, A/B kept as the quality check

data.alternatives: Wait for B-am-ingest: rejected, blocks every number.
data.decision: Interim read-only script with redacted aggregates only (no transcript text) is acceptable (operator 2026-10-23 accepted the defaults); it is replaced by the B-am-ingest reader when that lands and must not become a second transcript reader.
data.title: Interim measurement script, replaced by the B-am-ingest reader

data.alternatives: Free-form reports: rejected, lead context growth.
data.decision: At most 6 lines plus a pointer; detail in item evidence or scratch file; repeat wake-ups answer the delta only (operator 2026-10-23: 'Your defaults').
data.title: Subagent report: at most 6 lines plus a pointer

data.alternatives: Caps for everyone: rejected, hides data from the operator.
data.consequences: Agents must opt in to full output.
data.decision: --brief is the default when DDFLOW_AGENT is set; the operator's terminal stays unbounded; footer names the unbounded command (operator 2026-10-23: 'Your defaults').
data.title: Bounded output by default for agent shells

data.alternatives: Wait for the operator: rejected by the operator.
data.consequences: Spend resumes without a human; bounded by the daily cap; tasks TE-auto-resume, TE-spend-resume.
data.decision: Automatic resume, not wait-for-operator (operator 2026-10-23: 'check automatically if the limit is reset, and resume automatically if it is'). Tension recorded: this is a money decision the operator delegated; the proposal default was to wait. Needs: a limit-state source (parse the harness limit message incl. reset time, usage ledger B-gap-spend, per-agent-type budgets D-session-start-budget / LS-budget-per-agent); a timer/trigger (schedule resume at the reset time, poll sparsely); idempotent resume of all expired-lease agents in one command (relate D-orphan-recovery, DX-resume-command); safety knobs [spend].auto_resume = on, max resumes per day, quiet; a report in the operator digest.
data.title: After a spend-limit stop ddflow checks the reset and resumes automatically

data.alternatives: A only: drifts, no timing logic. C on Claude Code: no hook can compact.
data.consequences: No new MCP tool (D-mcp-new-nouns). Automatic lane rotation stays off until the operator turns it on; CC-window-extend and TE-Q2(b) are separate operator-requested behaviours.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. Option B (advisor, instruction seed, summary store, cache lint) delivered in four steps through existing channels; option C only for lane rotation and Pi.
data.title: Compaction option B: advisor, instruction seed, summary store, cache lint, in four steps

data.alternatives: Never touch the files: instruction seed would be unreachable.
data.consequences: Region edits by hand are overwritten; opt-out key per project.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. Marked, regenerated region written by ddflow setup; opt-out per project.
data.title: ddflow owns a marked '# Compact instructions' region in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md

data.alternatives: Block during merges by default: B195 rule, risks deadlock of a client that must compact.
data.consequences: A compaction during a merge is possible; resume pack re-grounds afterwards.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. Opt-in only via [compaction].block_during = ["merge"].
data.title: PreCompact never blocks by default

data.alternatives: Per-family tuning before measurement: rejected, data not available.
data.consequences: Thresholds are data per (harness, model family), not code; the operator-selected auto-compact window (D-TE-Q2) can override per run.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. Suggest/strong/rotate for lanes 150/250/350K, lead 250/400K, unknown family 150/250K; same values as TE-context-caps (one value, one knob; TE-Q2 lanes rotate at 250K).
data.title: Compaction thresholds: lanes 150/250/350K, lead 250/400K, unknown 150/250K

data.alternatives: Nudge every turn: noise and context cost.
data.consequences: A missed nudge is not repeated until the next level.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. Once per level, 20 minute cooldown, silent while waiting, off for the operator's own session unless asked.
data.title: Nudge budget: one per level, 20 min cooldown, silent while waiting

data.alternatives: Rotate automatically by default: rejected, operator keeps control.
data.consequences: Rotation depends on the lead acting on advice until enabled.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. Advise only; automatic lane rotation only after the operator turns it on. Note: CC-window-extend and TE-Q2(b) are separate operator-requested behaviours, not covered by this answer.
data.title: Subagent past the strong level: advise only

data.alternatives: Never store: loses anchors for search. Store raw: leak risk.
data.consequences: Displayed inside the data fence; nudges carry ids and numbers only.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. Store where readable, redacted before storage; pointer-only when opaque (Codex).
data.title: Store the harness's compaction summary, redacted; pointer-only when opaque

data.alternatives: Summaries on the 90-day transcript retention: loses provenance.
data.consequences: Log grows by summary size; redaction applied at write.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. Summaries are kept with the session log (D-no-deletion); chat turns follow the retention default (B-am-retention).
data.title: Stored summaries follow the session log; chat turns follow retention

data.alternatives: Keep-warm pings: dominated by 1h TTL, cost without benefit.
data.consequences: Gaps over an hour are cold; compaction at resume when cold and C >= 200K.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-23: 'Accept all nine defaults'. ddflow never polls to keep a cache warm; the 1h TTL setting (D-TE-Q1, TE-subagent-ttl) covers gaps under an hour.
data.title: No keep-warm polling; 1-hour TTL setting instead

data.body: WHAT: per client: is there a user-selectable compaction threshold or window (env, setting, flag, command), its range, precedence, read at launch or changeable at runtime, long-context model/mode availability by plan. Claude Code is verified: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW (100K-1M), autoCompactWindow, --autocompact, /autocompact; CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE lowers only. Output: a table with provenance and probe date (UNAVAILABLE not guessed), feeding CC-inventory and the ddflow/harnesses descriptors. WHY: D-TE-Q2 operator asked for a user-selectable window for every agent. TEST: every supported client has a row or an explicit unavailable.
data.title: Research: auto-compact window knobs for every coding agent ddflow supports (Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, Kilo/OpenCode, Aider, Kimi, Qwen, dsh, Pi, others in the client matrix); table

data.body: WHAT: from the CC-advisor fill estimate, task kind and remaining work, decide at launch or lane-rotation time to raise the auto-compact window (CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW) or pick a larger-context model/long-context mode where client and plan allow, until the task completes; warn the user via digest and brief. FEASIBILITY: a running client session usually cannot change its window mid-run (env/setting read at launch; Claude Code /autocompact is a user command), so the mechanism is launch/rotation-time from the estimate; for the lead it is a recommendation; per-agent knowledge of runtime change comes from TE-compact-window-per-agent. COST: larger windows cost more per call and per cache rewrite. SAFEGUARDS: [compaction].extend_ceiling knob, company floors tighten-only, off-by-default switch recorded in the warning. Operator-requested (D-TE-Q2 b); separate from automatic rotation (D-CC-Q6). TEST: fixture estimates over/under threshold choose window, ceiling clamps, unsupported client yields recommendation only.
data.title: Context-window extension: when the advisor estimates a task cannot finish before the compaction threshold, raise the effective window at launch or lane rotation, with a warning

data.body: WHAT: config table (layered: company floors, project, user) of price and spending limit/reset per model and subscription; the launcher picks a cheaper model, or one with headroom, for mechanical items; reviewers and design stay on the strongest available model satisfying the cross-family rule. WHY: D-TE-Q4 operator 2026-10-23. Links P-operator-digest (routing shown in digest), P-batch-gates, P-context-compaction. TEST: fixture table and usage pick the expected model; cross-family rule never violated; exhausted model skipped; UNAVAILABLE limit data is not treated as headroom.
data.title: Route work by remaining headroom per model/subscription with a layered price and limit table in config

data.body: WHAT: parse the harness limit message incl. reset time (limit-state source, plus usage ledger B-gap-spend and per-agent-type budgets D-session-start-budget/LS-budget-per-agent when present); schedule a resume at the reset time and poll sparsely; one idempotent command resumes all expired-lease agents (relate D-orphan-recovery, DX-resume-command, TE-spend-resume); safety: [spend].auto_resume = on, max resumes per day, quiet; report in the operator digest. WHY: D-TE-Q8, a money decision the operator delegated. TEST: fixture limit message to scheduled resume; second run is a no-op; daily cap stops it; limit not yet reset means no resume.
data.title: Detect a spend-limit stop, wait for the reset, resume all stopped agents automatically (capped)

data.body:
WHAT: first an A/B protocol in the item evidence (same task class, cheaper model vs current, record review rounds, ci failures, rework, units from TE-measure); only if rounds and rework do not rise by more than the price drop, add a per-role model key in the lane launch template (Claude Code subagent model: / CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL). WHY: every transcript is claude-sonnet-5-5, so nothing is measured (research section 2); fix lanes are 56% of subagent spend. Cross-family review rule unchanged. TEST: launch template renders the model; default unchanged.

AMENDED by D-TE-Q4 (operator 2026-10-23): no longer 'A/B first only'. Mechanical items route by headroom immediately via TE-limit-aware-routing; the measured A/B (20 mechanical fix items) stays as the quality check on rounds and rework. Reviewers and design stay strongest satisfying the cross-family rule.

WHAT: ONE data table keyed by model family (claude, openai, gemini, deepseek, kimi, qwen, glm, unknown): cache kind (explicit|automatic|none), ttl options, read/write multipliers, min cacheable tokens, window, compaction kind, each fact a three-valued record (status, source, date) in the HX-facts-core shape; plus per-harness capabilities the advisor needs (can run a compaction command, which hooks accept additionalContext, usage fields in transcripts, ttl env). Run and record the probes listed in research section 11 (hooks that reach subagents, PostCompact fields, PreCompact fields, Kimi/Codex caching). REUSE: HX-facts-core (fact shape), B-am-harness-probe ([transcripts] stays there), SU-client-table (client capabilities), research/mcp-client-matrix.md. Do not edit harnesses/*.toml. WHY: model family differs from harness (Claude Code can run non-Claude models); prices move so they are dated data, never code. TEST: every harness id has a row or an explicit unknown; every fact has source and date; a fact older than [context].facts_max_age_days makes doctor note it; unverified is never read as true. ACCEPTANCE: probe record per UNVERIFIED line of research section 11.

ADDED by D-TE-Q2: include the per-agent compact-window knob table from TE-compact-window-per-agent.

WHAT: a rotate hint (doctor/health and the wake brief) when an agent's context passes [session].agent_rotate_tokens (default 250000): finish the item, write the hand-off note into the item's evidence, stop; the lead starts a fresh agent that begins with ddflow brief. Driver delta documents CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW / CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE for agents and the lead. WHY: research 3.3: 12 agents with 300+ calls = 67% of subagent spend, 39 grew over 200 K; model saves ~40% on top of the 1-hour TTL; lead median context 402 K, one compaction at 967 K. TEST: hint fires at the threshold from fixture usage; hand-off note round-trips through ddflow brief. FALSIFIER: rotated lanes need more review rounds or more rework (compare ddflow metrics, 20 items each). Links LS-budget-per-agent (start size) without touching its files.

AMENDED by D-TE-Q2: also expose the user-selectable auto-compact window (Claude Code CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW/autoCompactWindow/--autocompact) as an alternative to rotation; per-agent equivalents from TE-compact-window-per-agent; window extension is CC-window-extend.

WHAT: agents that hit 'monthly spend limit' record a one-line state; ddflow lists the stopped ones and emits one resume text for the lead to broadcast. WHY: research 3.3: 15 subagent runs and 2 lead turns hit the limit; resume rewrites 5.5 M tokens (1% of spend) plus per-agent nudges. Reuse B-quota-pause, do not build a second pause path. TEST: fixture limit message to stopped list to resume text.

AMENDED by D-TE-Q8: automatic resume at the reset is TE-auto-resume; this task keeps the one-command manual resume text.

WHAT: ddflow wait and the driver's poll recipes never block longer than [wait].max_call_seconds (default 240) and return a still-waiting result the agent re-calls; heartbeat rides on it; the driver text stops teaching 'for i in seq; sleep 8..20' loops capped near 570 s. WHY: research 3.3: 583 rewrite events (163 M tokens, 31% of subagent spend) follow claim/heartbeat+sleep loops averaging 11.7 min; ten minutes waited as one call costs ~4x three short calls. Fallback for hosts that cannot use TE-subagent-ttl. TEST: wait with a held file returns at <=240 s with exit 2-style still-waiting; no busy loop; heartbeat renewed.

AMENDED by D-TE-Q3: the 240 s cap applies always, not only as fallback.

WHAT: the launch brief ends with a report template (verdict, item ids, outcome per gate, blockers, pointer to evidence/file; at most 6 lines; no tables; repeat wake-ups give only what changed). Driver gets lead habits: no repeated tables, no re-listing, bounded commands, fewer nudges. WHY: research 3.2: subagent reports are 23% of what the lead adds (avg 785 tokens, 226 reports) and 20% of its carry cost; 62% come from agents that reported more than once. Saving small (0.5-1% of total) but slows lead growth. REUSE: P-operator-digest owns the operator-side digest; this is the agent-to-lead side. TEST: brief contains the template within the LS-launch-brief-budget budget; template lint on a fixture report.

D-TE-Q6/Q7 defaults: <=6 lines plus pointer; agent shells get bounded --brief by default, terminal unbounded.

data.summary: D-labels and D-wave-semantics say 'ddflow waves --stamp' derives wave:N tags, but 'ddflow waves' is not a command (invalid choice) and tasks carry no wave: tags, so the wave convention cannot be followed when filing tasks. Also: no command checks the existing graph for needs cycles (only plan check on proposals); 'ddflow gate skip' printed no approval id.
data.title: ddflow waves --stamp from D-labels/D-wave-semantics does not exist

data.body:
Fixes bug B47acb25115: D-labels and D-wave-semantics say 'ddflow waves --stamp' derives wave:N tags, but 'ddflow waves' is not a command (invalid choice) and tasks carry no wave: tags, so the wave convention cannot be followed when filing tasks. Also: no command checks the existing graph for needs cycles (only plan check on proposals); 'ddflow gate skip' printed no approval id. Found on TE-decide.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B47acb25115 --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B47acb25115 --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B47acb25115: ddflow waves --stamp from D-labels/D-wave-semantics does not exist
